item.title: Symmetry-Broken Coordination of Single-Atom Catalysts Unlocks Spin- and Orbital-Regulated Sulfur Redox in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in creating asymmetric Cl–Co–N3 single-atom catalysts that induce a low-to-high spin transition in Co(II), tuning dz2–π* hybridization and d-band occupancy to accelerate polysulfide conversion. This spin/orbital engineering strategy significantly boosts sulfur redox kinetics, enabling lithium–sulfur batteries with exceptional cycling stability (0.023% fade per cycle), offering a general design principle for advanced catalysts.

Significance: this enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, with a Sn/MgCl2 interface preventing anode passivation—establishing a general principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in high-energy magnesium batteries.

item.title: Manipulating Li2MnO3-Like Domain Dispersion in Lithium-Rich Layered Oxides Inherited from Precursor
item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in establishing that precursor transition-metal separation templates Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion in lithium-rich cathodes—clustered precursors yield localized ordering, less-ordered precursors yield dispersed ordering. item.title: Water serves as a charge-transfer medium for ultrafast aqueous batteries
item.description:

Nature Reviews Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Perspective proposes interfacial water as a charge-transfer medium in aqueous batteries, explaining ultrafast kinetics via water cleavage and reorganization at electrode–electrolyte interfaces. It reframes charge storage beyond ion-centric models, links water-derived protons and transient intermediates to observed signatures, and outlines mechanisms, tunability, characterization, and design implications for high-power aqueous energy storage.

item.title: In Situ Hetero-Layered Quasi-Solid-State Electrolyte Enable Enhanced Ion Transport for Safe Sodium Metal Batteries

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an in situ-formed hetero-layered quasi-solid-state electrolyte that creates seamless solid-solid contact and enhances ion transport. Its significance is enabling safe, high-energy-density sodium metal batteries by overcoming the interfacial and conductivity limitations of conventional solid electrolytes, offering a practical route to next-generation energy storage.

item.title: p-Block metal-induced p–d orbital hybridization enhances the oxygen reduction performance of an Fe–N–C catalyst in zinc–air batteries
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using p-block metal In to induce p–d orbital hybridization in an Fe–N–C catalyst, tuning its electronic structure. This significantly boosts oxygen reduction activity and zinc–air battery performance, achieving stable open-circuit voltage and high peak power density. It offers a viable strategy for designing efficient, durable non-precious-metal catalysts for energy devices.
🏷 Fe-N-C catalyst · oxygen reduction · zinc-air battery · p-d hybridization · indium doping
